hints: Use the partial-fraction form $\dfrac{A}{3-x}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{1+3x^2}$ because the denominator has one linear and one irreducible quadratic factor.
Equate the constant, $x$ and $x^2$ coefficients, or substitute convenient values, and then insert the three constants into the decomposition.
walkthrough: Use a correct method to find a constant

hints: Integrate the two partial fractions from part (a) separately over $0\le x\le1$.
Use $\int\dfrac{2}{3-x}\,dx=-2\ln(3-x)$ and rewrite $\dfrac1{1+3x^2}$ in the standard arctangent form with $u=\sqrt3x$.
Evaluate both antiderivatives at $1$ and $0$, using $\tan^{-1}(\sqrt3)=\pi/3$, then combine and simplify the logarithms exactly.
